rounds.text: Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a P/E of 21.4x [E1] while offering exceptional profitability metrics that tower above sector benchmarks, including an ROE of 24.14% versus the sector's 8.67% [E9] and an ROCE of 19.65% against a sector benchmark of 10.27% [E10]. The business is compounding its fundamentals at an elite pace, highlighted by a compounded profit growth of 189% over the trailing twelve months [E21] and a 36% CAGR over the last five years [E19], supported by strategic retail network expansion and in-house diamond manufacturing for higher margins [E76, E77]. This operational excellence is reinforced by a discounted cash flow model showing an intrinsic value of Rs 1295 per share alongside a generous margin of safety of 47.6% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that today's price requires a modest 9.1% earnings growth, which is easily eclipsed by the base case assumption of 18.0% [E47]. Technical momentum confirms this strength, with a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 and the price positioned firmly above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50, E51]. Conceded: the stock trades at 5.65x P/B against a sector benchmark of 1.96x [E7], debt to equity stands at 1.06x [E37], and institutional money flow reflects negative sentiment with a holding change of -0.77 percentage points [E44].

The evidence reveals material balance sheet vulnerabilities and valuation disconnects that caution against uncritical acceptance of recent performance. Leverage is high, with debt exceeding net worth at a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.06x, and total borrowings expanding to Rs 886 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 792 Cr a year prior [E37, E39]. This debt expansion coincides with a deeply concerning cash conversion ratio of just 0.15x for March 2026, pointing to reported profits sitting far ahead of actual cash generation and signaling potential risks in receivables or accruals [E34]. Furthermore, institutional conviction is heading in the wrong direction, evidenced by negative money flow and foreign institutional holdings dropping by 1.37 percentage points to 0.45% [E42, E44], while screen reasons flag active deceleration in earnings growth [E68]. Valuation multiples also appear stretched compared to sector peers, with the price-to-book ratio standing at an elevated 5.65x against a sector benchmark of 1.96x [E7], and the EV/EBITDA trading slightly above sector norms at 14.61x [E11]. The stock's extreme volatility of 56.5% and a brutal historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -93.4% underscore the severe downside risks embedded in holding this name [E53, E54]. Conceded: [E45].

The bear's alarm over leverage ignores that TBZ's exceptional profitability—highlighted by an ROE of 24.14% and ROCE of 19.65% crushing sector benchmarks—generates robust operational returns [E9, E10]. While borrowings expanded to ₹886 Cr, the company simultaneously produced ₹30 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹16 Cr in free cash flow, while driving top-line revenue up 22.23% via strong retail execution [E35, E36, E39, E75]. The concern over the 0.15x cash conversion ratio [E34] is substantially mitigated by the company's rules-based screen scoring a high 90 out of 100 with a medium-confidence BUY rating [E63]. Furthermore, the premium price-to-book multiple of 5.65x [E7] is entirely justified when viewed against an impressive earnings growth engine that delivered 189% TTM profit growth and a 36% 5-year CAGR [E19, E21]. Conceded: [E42, E53, E68].

The bull relies heavily on impressive ROE and ROCE figures [E9, E10], but fails to address the glaring operational reality that reported profits are entirely disconnected from actual liquidity, as evidenced by a severe cash conversion ratio of just 0.15x for March 2026 [E34]. While the bull dismisses leverage concerns using operating cash flow and free cash flow metrics [E35, E36], borrowings have actually expanded to ₹886 Cr—pushing the debt-to-equity ratio to 1.06x, meaning debt officially exceeds the company's net worth [E37, E39]. Conceded: [E19, E21, E75]. Furthermore, leaning on a rules-based screen score [E63] ignores the system's own explicit warnings that earnings growth is actively decelerating and institutional money is flowing out through negative money flow [E44, E68, E69]. Finally, attempting to justify a hefty 5.65x price-to-book multiple [E7] ignores that the historical median ROE over a ten-year span sits at a modest 9% [E26], proving that cyclical volatility [E58] makes peak multiples a dangerous baseline for investors.

The bear points to a cash conversion ratio of 0.15x for March 2026 [E34], but completely ignores that the business still generated absolute operating cash flow of Rs 30 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 16 Cr in that same period [E35, E36]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio sits at 1.06x with borrowings at ₹886 Cr [E37, E39], yet the company's operational execution is driving exceptional fundamentals, including a 19% 5-year sales CAGR [E15] and a 36% 5-year profit CAGR [E19] alongside a robust revenue growth of 22.23% in FY26 supported by retail expansion [E75, E76]. While the bear highlights institutional outflows and a decelerating growth warning [E44, E68, E69], the quantitative rules-based screen still awards the stock a high confidence score of 90 out of 100 on the back of 35% YoY sales growth and 55% YoY net profit growth [E63, E64, E66]. Finally, dismissing the valuation multiple based on a 10-year median ROE of 9% [E26] ignores the dramatic structural re-rating and current profitability surge, featuring a TTM ROE of 27.1% [E13] and a median ROE of 27% over the last year [E29].

Conceded: the company generated absolute operating cash flow of Rs 30 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 16 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], but a cash conversion ratio of 0.15x proves that reported profits are severely detached from actual cash generation, pointing directly to receivables and accrual risks [E34]. While the bull points to a 19% 5-year sales CAGR [E15] and 36% 5-year profit growth [E19] alongside fiscal retail expansion [E75, E76], the rules-based screen explicitly flags that earnings growth is decelerating and institutional money flow remains negative with institutional holdings dropping to 0.45% [E42, E44, E68, E69]. The high confidence screen score [E63] fails to offset the structural vulnerability of a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.06x with borrowings expanding to Rs 886 Cr [E37, E39], putting the company's leverage above net worth. Finally, while the bull cites a TTM ROE of 27.1% [E13], relying on this recent surge ignores the 10-year median ROE of just 9% [E26] and an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend over the last two years [E32].
